claims.statement: KSeF receipt became mandatory from 1 February 2026; mandatory issuance began for the largest taxpayers on that date and for most others on 1 April 2026, with a temporary small-invoice exception through 2026.
KSeF has several offline procedures with different deadlines and document-delivery or QR rules, creating exception states that must be tracked.
The Ministry publishes KSeF 2.0 OpenAPI contracts and integration environments, making an independent monitor technically testable.
Accounting offices will buy an independent control layer rather than rely on their ERP and free government applications.

contrary_evidence: The Ministry offers free KSeF applications, and established ERP or accounting vendors can add similar controls.
The product handles tax-sensitive data and could create liability if users treat alerts as tax advice.
The 2026 exception regime means not every invoice belongs in KSeF, increasing false-positive risk.

economics.acquisition_route: Sell first through two accounting offices that can aggregate many end clients, using the official test environment and an offline or self-hosted option for sensitive data.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable ERP mappings, exception rules and a test corpus of non-sensitive failure cases can lower onboarding cost. Incumbent ERP vendors can replicate features, so speed and neutrality across systems matter more than data possession.
fingerprint.customer: Polish accounting offices and multi-system SMEs that already have invoice software but need an independent control over KSeF receipts, offline invoices, acknowledgements and ERP or bank reconciliation.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Sell first through two accounting offices that can aggregate many end clients, using the official test environment and an offline or self-hosted option for sensitive data.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A read-only exception monitor imports KSeF status and internal invoice identifiers, flags missing UPO or KSeF numbers, duplicate documents, overdue offline sends and receipt gaps, and exports a close checklist. It complements rather than replaces invoicing software.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The accounting office or finance team pays per connected tax entity each month after a sandbox proof and reconciliation report; a one-time onboarding fee covers mappings and permissions.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An invoice is created or received during normal, offline24, maintenance or outage handling and finance staff must prove that it reached KSeF on time, was not duplicated and matches internal records.

founder_fit: Structured-data reconciliation fits the founder's data and finance orientation
Accounting-office distribution aggregates customers and reduces repeated selling
A read-only monitor is safer than becoming the system of record
Official test APIs enable a low-capital MVP
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: KSeF offline-queue and reconciliation control for accounting offices
uncertainties: Real exception rates after the first implementation wave
API permissions and throttling for accounting offices serving many taxpayers
Security requirements and preference for self-hosting
Price that is lower than avoided reconciliation labor yet supports integration
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Build against the official integration environment, simulate all published offline states, and run a read-only four-week pilot with one accounting office and two SMEs. Compare alerts with manual close, measure minutes saved and false positives, and require a paid per-entity renewal before adding another ERP connector.
